fact_sheet.business_description: General Re is a major reinsurer providing risk capacity to insurers in the United States and internationally, including interests in Cologne Re [D01]. Its business combines underwriting with a large invested-asset pool and includes a financial-products operation with exposures differing from traditional property-casualty reinsurance [D01].
products_customers_and_why_they_buy: Provides risk capacity to other insurers [D01].
Product includes traditional property-casualty reinsurance and financial-products/derivatives [D01, D05].
Repeat-purchase/loyalty evidence: Reinsurance relationships can appear entrenched but may disappear if customers find better service or lower prices elsewhere [D01].
economics: Investment balance is only valuable if underwriting cost is acceptable; inadequate pricing or underestimated reserves can create non-existent reported profits [D01].
Capital intensity: Highly capital-intensive; regulatory capital and claims-paying ability constrain investment in equities or distributions to owners [D01, D06].
earnings_record: Cyclicality: Underwriting performance is subject to industry cycles; international premium growth reflected consolidation [D06].
competitive_position: Major reinsurer, not a new venture [D03].
Durable competitive advantage is not guaranteed; a recognizable name is not sufficient evidence of an economic franchise [D01].
Competes on price, expertise, reliability, and financial strength [D06].
balance_sheet_and_capital_needs: Float/Obligations: Premiums received before claims are paid create investment funds but also carry future obligations [D02, D08].
management_and_capital_allocation: Record: Maintained high operating ROE in recent years [D06].
Capital allocation: Utilizes float from reinsurance operations for investment [D01].
price_and_valuation: Proposed consideration: $276.50 per share based on announcement terms [D04].
what_the_market_is_worried_about: Reserve estimates may be insufficient and underpricing may surface slowly [D05].
Financial-products book introduces valuation and liquidity risks [D05].
International subsidiaries add currency, legal, and counterparty complexity [D05].
deal_terms_if_any: All-stock transaction valued at approximately $22 billion [D02, D09].
Exchange ratio: 0.0035 Berkshire Class A shares or 0.105 Class B shares for each General Re share [D02, D09].
recent_events: June 19, 1998: Announcement of proposed merger with Berkshire Hathaway [D01, D07].
berkshire_context: Proposed acquisition is a whole-company purchase through Berkshire stock [D01].
Berkshire has significant existing stock portfolio, though not cash for merger [D08].
The idea of an internal comparison is noted, though Berkshire's own insurance lines/capital needs differ [D06].
missing_data: Fully reconciled latest loss-reserve schedule [D02, D09].

understandable.evidence: The business is a major, long-established reinsurer whose core function of providing risk capacity is well-understood, despite risks inherent in the financial products book [D01, D03, D05].

durable_moat_and_pricing_power.evidence: As a major player with high financial strength, it possesses the necessary scale and capital to compete effectively in reinsurance, even if the advantage is not guaranteed [D01, D06].

consistent_earnings_record.evidence: Net income has grown consistently from $711 million in 1993 to $968 million in 1997 [D02].

high_roe_little_debt.evidence: The company has maintained strong operating ROE in the 14.5% to 16.9% range with very low long-term debt relative to its invested asset base [D02, D06].

capital_intensity.evidence: The business is highly capital-intensive and regulatory requirements constrain the deployment of its capital [D01, D06].

able_honest_owner_minded_management.evidence: Management has successfully maintained high operating returns and effective float utilization [D06].

size_moves_the_needle.evidence: The $22 billion transaction size is clearly meaningful for Berkshire Hathaway [D02, D09].

price_screen.evidence: The earnings yield of 4.43% is significantly below the 1.5x long-term bond yield benchmark (approx. 8.2%) and lower than the 5.47% 10-year Treasury yield [D04].

gate1.one_line_business_quality_verdict: a high-quality, capital-intensive reinsurance franchise with strong underwriting records but limited pricing protection at the current valuation

gate2.why_available: The market views this as a standard corporate merger at a premium to book value, rather than a bargain opportunity. We see the value in acquiring a massive, high-quality float generator that fits perfectly into the Berkshire model of permanent capital, despite the immediate earnings yield appearing high relative to our typical valuation targets [D01, D08].
evidence: Proposed all-stock merger valued at approximately $22 billion [D02, D09]
General Re possesses a large, durable pool of investable float [D01, D02]
Consistent operating ROE exceeding 14% over the last five years [D02]
gate2.market_narrative_we_disagree_with: The market focuses on the short-term earnings yield of 4.43% and the potential volatility within the financial-products book [D04, D05].
what_must_be_true: Reserve estimates for claims must be conservative and accurate
The financial-products book must not contain hidden, catastrophic tail risk
The combined entity must maintain its underwriting discipline to ensure the cost of float remains low over the long term

gate3.owner_earnings_per_share: Not strictly applicable due to insurer float model; 1997 net income $968M [D02] / 78.4M shares = $12.35 EPS [D04]

intrinsic_value_range.low: Book value $109.11/share [D04] plus franchise value of float
intrinsic_value_range.high: Estimated value of recurring float generation and underwriting power
key_assumptions: Float grows at or above long bond rate [D01]

gate3.price_vs_value: Price 2.53x book [D04]; justified if float exceeds 2.5x book in value and underwriting risk is managed
gate3.alternatives: Existing stock portfolio or T-bills; this deal provides unique permanent float which Berkshire can deploy at higher rates than Gen Re [D01, D08]
gate3.downside_case: Overestimation of reserve adequacy leading to capital impairment; permanent loss if underwriting discipline fails [D01, D05]
flagged_assumptions: Assumed float value equals face value for long-term holders
Assumed Berkshire stock used as currency is undervalued at exchange time

gate4.role_description: We are acquiring General Re as a whole company, leaving management in place to continue their underwriting discipline while redirecting their significant float to Omaha for more effective capital allocation [D01, D08].
value_realisation_path: Acquisition of high-quality, durable insurance float [D01]
Improved capital deployment of Gen Re's assets through Berkshire's investment expertise [D01, D08]
Synergistic underwriting integration over the long term [D01]
gate4.why_this_role_fits_the_era: In the 1980-1999 era, we focus on purchasing whole companies at scale to secure reliable long-term insurance float, which serves as a vital engine for Berkshire's compounding [D01, D02].

kill_criteria: Underwriting discipline fails, leading to recurring underwriting losses and expensive float
Reserve estimates prove significantly inadequate, leading to capital impairment
Financial-products book contains hidden, catastrophic tail risk
Management expands outside of reinsurance and core insurance-related competencies
gate5.berkshire_constraints: The acquisition is a $22 billion whole-company merger using Berkshire stock, which must not compromise our reputation for financial strength or prudent underwriting [D01, D02, D09].
gate5.opportunity_cost: Comparison with alternative deployments of capital into the equity market or internal growth; however, this deal provides permanent access to General Re's massive, high-quality float that cannot be replicated through simple stock purchases [D01, D08].
gate5.leverage: None beyond the implicit leverage associated with insurance float and minor long-term debt [D02].
gate5.decider_reason: This is a major, negotiated whole-company acquisition of a significant insurance franchise that fits perfectly within Berkshire's circle of competence and capital-allocation strategy.
gate5.biggest_risk_in_one_sentence: The primary risk is a latent, large-scale misestimation of loss reserves or an unforeseen disaster in the financial-products book that could impair capital and reputation.

valuation.intrinsic_value_range: Book value of $109.11/share plus the capitalized value of durable, low-cost insurance float.
valuation.downside_case: Significant underestimation of loss reserves or catastrophic failure in the financial-products book leading to capital impairment.

drivers.driver: The acquisition offers a permanent, massive pool of insurance float that far exceeds our ability to replicate in the open market, providing the fundamental engine for Berkshire’s long-term compounding [D01, D08].
General Re is a premier global reinsurer with an excellent record of underwriting discipline and operating ROEs consistently between 14.5% and 16.9% [D02, D06].

By acquiring the entire business, we gain the ability to redirect the massive investable asset base into our own superior investment allocation strategy, creating value beyond the standalone reinsurance entity [D01, D08].
Management has proven its ability to operate effectively within a capital-intensive industry while maintaining a balance sheet with very little long-term debt [D02, D06].

kill_criteria: Underwriting discipline fails, leading to recurring underwriting losses and expensive float
Reserve estimates prove significantly inadequate, leading to capital impairment
Financial-products book contains hidden, catastrophic tail risk
Management expands outside of reinsurance and core insurance-related competencies
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that General Re's loss reserves are fundamentally inadequate or that the financial-products book contains hidden risks that threaten the permanence of their float.
final.memo:
Charlie and I have long admired General Re, and we are pleased to welcome them into the Berkshire family. This business is a giant in the reinsurance industry, providing the essential risk capacity that global insurers rely upon to operate [D01, D03]. We understand this industry well, and in General Re, we see a company that has built a formidable reputation for financial strength and underwriting expertise [D01, D06].

General Re has delivered a stellar record, with operating returns on equity consistently in the 14.5% to 16.9% range over the past five years [D02, D06]. Their business is highly capital-intensive, which is exactly why they have maintained such a disciplined balance sheet with very little long-term debt [D02, D06]. By combining this operational excellence with our own investment approach, we believe we can utilize their massive float far more effectively than it has been in the past [D01, D08].

The market currently views this transaction through the narrow lens of short-term earnings multiples and a 4.43% earnings yield [D04, D05]. What the market misses is that we are not buying a simple stream of quarterly earnings; we are acquiring a permanent source of low-cost capital [D01, D08]. The price we are paying, at 2.53 times book value, is fair when one considers the durable, long-term value of the float this franchise generates [D04].

We recognize the risks: reinsurance is a cyclical business, and the financial-products book requires constant vigilance [D01, D05, D06]. We are not looking for a quick turnaround; we are looking for a business that we can hold indefinitely [D01, D04]. Our commitment to General Re is absolute, provided their underwriting discipline remains as sharp as it has been throughout their history [D01, D05].
